subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me a challenging KS3 exam-style question on {lo}, then mark my answer.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for KS3 simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake.
learningObjectives: Angle sums of triangles and polygons

questions.q: A rectangle is 7 cm long and 3 cm wide. What is its perimeter?
questions.explain: Perimeter adds all four sides: 7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20 cm. (21 cm would be the area, and 42 cm doubles it wrongly.)

questions.q: What is the area of a rectangle measuring 6 cm by 4 cm?
questions.explain: Area = length × width = 6 × 4 = 24 cm². Area is in square units (cm²), not cm.

questions.q: Which measurement tells you how much flat space is inside a 2-D shape?
questions.explain: Area is the space inside a 2-D shape. Perimeter is the distance around the edge, and volume is for 3-D solids.

questions.q: A triangle has a base of 10 cm and a perpendicular height of 8 cm. What is its area?
questions.explain: Area of a triangle = ½ × base × height = ½ × 10 × 8 = 40 cm². Forgetting the ½ gives 80 cm².

questions.q: In the triangle area formula ½ × base × height, which length must the height be?
questions.explain: The height must be the perpendicular distance from the base to the opposite vertex — not a slanted side.

questions.q: A cuboid measures 5 cm by 3 cm by 2 cm. What is its volume?
questions.explain: Volume of a cuboid = length × width × height = 5 × 3 × 2 = 30 cm³. Volume uses cubic units (cm³).

questions.q: Which units are used to measure volume?
questions.explain: Volume is measured in cubic units such as cm³, because it fills 3-D space.

questions.q: Two angles sit together on a straight line. One is 115°. What is the other?
questions.explain: Angles on a straight line add up to 180°, so the other angle is 180 − 115 = 65°.

questions.q: Three angles meet at a point. Two of them are 90° and 130°. What is the third?
questions.explain: Angles around a point add to 360°: 360 − 90 − 130 = 140°.

questions.q: When two straight lines cross, what is true of vertically opposite angles?
questions.explain: Vertically opposite angles (across the X where two lines cross) are always equal to each other.

questions.lo: Angle sums of triangles and polygons
questions.q: Two angles of a triangle are 55° and 65°. What is the third angle?
questions.explain: Angles in a triangle add to 180°: 180 − 55 − 65 = 60°. A common error is using 360° instead of 180°.

questions.lo: Angle sums of triangles and polygons
questions.q: Using (n − 2) × 180°, what is the sum of the interior angles of a pentagon (5 sides)?
questions.explain: (5 − 2) × 180 = 3 × 180 = 540°. A pentagon splits into three triangles.

questions.lo: Angle sums of triangles and polygons
questions.q: What do the interior angles of any quadrilateral add up to?
questions.explain: (4 − 2) × 180 = 360°. A quadrilateral splits into two triangles, each 180°.

questions.q: How many faces, edges and vertices does a cube have?
questions.explain: A cube has 6 faces, 12 edges and 8 vertices (corners).

questions.q: Two shapes are exactly the same shape and the same size. What are they called?
questions.explain: Congruent shapes are identical in shape and size. Similar shapes are the same shape but a different size.

questions.q: A shape is slid 3 squares right and 1 square down without turning or flipping. Which transformation is this?
questions.explain: Sliding a shape without turning, flipping or resizing is a translation.

questions.q: Which transformation flips a shape across a mirror line?
questions.explain: A reflection flips a shape across a mirror line, so the image is a mirror-image of the original.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides 3 cm and 4 cm. How long is the hypotenuse?
In a right-angled triangle, where is the hypotenuse?
questions.explain: The hypotenuse is the longest side and is always opposite the right angle.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has shorter sides 5 cm and 12 cm. How long is the hypotenuse?
